player_0.content: New plan: I failed because I misinterpreted the logical structure of Premise 3. I treated "Being a close friend of Shanika is necessary for being a close friend of Francine" as $F \rightarrow S$, but the correct translation of "X is necessary for Y" is $Y \rightarrow X$ (i.e., $F \rightarrow S$ is actually correct in my notation, but I failed to realize that Premise 2 ($F \rightarrow C$) combined with Premise 1 ($F \rightarrow C \lor A \lor S$) makes the disjunction redundant and provides no information about $A$). Specifically, knowing $F$ implies $C$ makes the condition $(C \lor A \lor S)$ always true for any $F$, rendering $A$ irrelevant to the truth of $F$. I should have immediately recognized that Premise 2 alone is sufficient to satisfy Premise 1 for any $F$, meaning $A$ is never forced to be true. Next time, I will strictly translate "necessary for" as "if consequent then antecedent" and check if any premise makes the disjunction in another premise redundant before concluding validity.
